static_traits.name: Tang Sikai
static_traits.family_status: Lives alone with a poodle, Nanette
static_traits.social_status: Has several close friends in New York to talk with, but has not yet sought their support on this issue
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; has not received other psychotherapy; no history of similar problems
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, logic fairly coherent, attitude neutral, able to self-reflect, fairly high cooperativeness

basic_info.main_problem: I often feel I am the worst dog owner because I forgot to pet my poodle Nanette before going to work on Wall Street, leading to guilt, self-criticism, and feelings of inadequacy.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent guilt and self-criticism begin to affect mood and work focus, and therefore seeks counseling
growth_experiences: A few months ago, the client adopted a poodle, Nanette; at first, the stress was relatively high due to adjusting to a new routine of living with a pet; as time passed the problem worsened, especially on busy workdays when the client easily forgot simple tasks (such as petting Nanette before leaving home), resulting in guilt and self-criticism almost every day, affecting work focus, sleep, and eating.

core_beliefs: I am the worst dog owner
If I make a small mistake in caregiving, I will fail in other areas as well

special_situations.event: On a busy workday, forgot to pet Nanette before going out to work on Wall Street
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot even remember such a small detail, it means I am neglecting her and I am a bad owner
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ruminates all day and reminds the self of the care and love once given, hoping to relieve guilt in this way
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is a disaster; I am the worst dog owner

special_situations.event: When small mistakes occur in life or simple tasks are forgotten
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If one mishap occurs, it indicates overall failure and all efforts are erased
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Using negative labels for self-criticism to force oneself to be more cautious

special_situations.event: At work, attention is disturbed by the thought 'I am a bad owner'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot take good care of my pet, it means I am no good in other areas either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly thinking at work and trying to self-correct, in order to regain a sense of control
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot even take care of a pet well; my work will fail too

special_situations.event: Thinking of after forgetting to pet, associating Nanette's feelings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I forget to pet her, she will definitely be disappointed and hurt because of it
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Not discussing these feelings with friends, choosing to bear them alone to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: She must be very disappointed; I am hurting her

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as a responsible, warm, and competent caregiver (love for the pet and a sense of worth)
core_conflict.fear: Fears being negated as a 'bad owner' because of one oversight, and extending this to a failure of the whole self
defense_goal: Maintains high standards and avoids making mistakes again by strengthening self-monitoring and self-reproach, thereby reducing the risk of being negated

object_relations.self_representation: A guilty caregiver who may fail
object_relations.object_representation: A pet that is easily hurt by me and would be disappointed in me

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When realizing they forgot to pet the pet before going out, or when thoughts at work remind them of this oversight
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Equates one oversight with total failure, and positions the self as a 'bad owner'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses a self-blaming tone and absolute words (such as 'the worst'), ignores positive evidence, and reinforces negative labels.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes reframing the perspective or assigns homework to identify and rewrite catastrophic thoughts
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tends to handle things through rational analysis, weakening emotional contact, trying to control unease through planning and logic
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responds in calm, rational, planned language, emphasizing methods and steps, reducing emotional expression.

manifestations: After adopting a pet, highly sensitive to the issue of 'choice comes with responsibility'
Worrying that one oversight means one has failed in one's duty
Forgetting details in a busy daily life triggers ongoing self-judgment
Living alone
Although there are a few friends, has not sought support or shared about this problem
outcomes: Emotional burden hard to relieve, slow recovery

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Evaluating oneself with absolutist labels such as 'the worst dog owner'
Regards 'must pet the pet before every outing' as an inviolable rigid standard

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Does not discuss this kind of guilt with friends; chooses to bear it alone
Turning the energy for coping with mistakes into self-blame and self-criticism

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive reproach over and vigilance about tiny mistakes
Frequently evaluates oneself with negative labels and worries about total failure

positive_force: Has a strong sense of responsibility and care for the pet (feeding, daily walks, accompanying play)
Has the ability for rational reflection and is willing to try cognitive restructuring
Having some social support resources (several friends in New York)
Proactively seeking professional help, good motivation
negative_force: Catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking are prominent
Ruminating on guilt leads to distracted attention and low mood
Work pressure and a busy schedule increase the likelihood of forgetting and mistakes
Sleep and eating rhythms are impaired; recovery and regulation capacity decline

target_behavior.behavior: Feels persistent guilt and self-criticism (rumination) over the event of forgetting to pet the pet
antecedent: Forgetting to pet Nanette before going out to work on Wall Street
Any tiny mistake in life or forgetting a simple task
target_behavior.core_reason: Perfectionistic and catastrophizing cognitions about caregiving, worrying about disappointing the pet, extending a single mistake to overall failure and internalizing it as high-standard self-demands
target_behavior.function: Obtains a sense of control through self-blame and excessive vigilance and avoids making mistakes again (escaping the risk of uncertainty and being negated)
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood, decreased work attention, disturbed sleep and eating rhythms
